claim: Static pre-trained ASR models exhibit significant performance disparities across L1 accent groups
safe_wording: All evaluated static models show substantial baseline accent disparities across speech variety strata (e.g. South Asian English consistently experiences 2x to 3x higher WER than Canadian or Irish English).
unsupported_or_overclaimed_wording: Static ASR models are inherently biased against foreign speakers.

claim: Continual test-time entropy adaptation (SUTA) causes positive aggregate WER regression under real-world accent shift
safe_wording: Positive aggregate WER regression was observed under unconstrained SUTA for all six evaluated CTC backbones under the frozen Common Voice 27.0 evaluation stream.
unsupported_or_overclaimed_wording: SUTA universally causes catastrophic failure on all speech datasets.

claim: Continual adaptation can induce localized subgroup regression without increasing whole-population disparity spread
safe_wording: Under severe acoustic and accent shifts, specific subgroups experienced acute regression while global disparity range remained flat or contracted due to elevated baseline error floors across all groups.

claim: The Disparity Safety Gate (DSG) acts as a conservative empirical candidate-update risk screen
safe_wording: DSG provides a conservative empirical candidate-update risk-screening mechanism that consistently reduced or prevented observed SUTA regression across all six evaluated CTC backbones.
unsupported_or_overclaimed_wording: DSG guarantees universal safety and mathematical fairness.

claim: DSG acceptance rate is model-dependent rather than uniform
safe_wording: Under identical frozen risk thresholds, controller acceptance rate ranged from 0.0% (XLSR) to 4.0% (Wav2Vec2-base), reflecting model-dependent alignment between candidate gradient updates and the sentinel panel.
unsupported_or_overclaimed_wording: DSG operates identically on all neural network architectures.

claim: Rejection of 225/225 candidates on XLSR-53 represents successful safety screening with zero adaptation utilization
safe_wording: On XLSR-53, DSG rejected all 225 candidate updates under frozen sentinel criteria, completely preventing the +2.73 pp external SUTA degradation while yielding zero adaptation utilization.

claim: Pretraining diversity in Wav2Vec2-large-robust is associated with lower SUTA regression than Libri-Light LV60
safe_wording: The multi-domain robustly fine-tuned checkpoint exhibited lower observed SUTA regression than the LV60 checkpoint (+0.37 pp vs +1.04 pp), consistent with greater robustness, though pretraining diversity cannot be isolated as a causal factor.
unsupported_or_overclaimed_wording: Diverse pretraining causes immunity to test-time adaptation degradation.

claim: Candidate sentinel non-inferiority does not guarantee downstream external stream benefit
safe_wording: The independent sentinel panel provides conservative empirical risk screening, but sentinel performance is not a perfect predictor of downstream external-stream behavior due to distribution shift.
unsupported_or_overclaimed_wording: Sentinel evaluation perfectly predicts all future test-stream outcomes.

claim: Autoregressive Seq2Seq models (Whisper) are mathematically incompatible with CTC frame-entropy SUTA
safe_wording: Because autoregressive sequence-to-sequence models generate tokens sequentially without frame-synchronous categorical emissions, the specific frame-entropy CTC adaptation protocol is mathematically non-applicable.
unsupported_or_overclaimed_wording: Seq2Seq models can never be adapted at test time.

claim: Zero fail-closed software errors occurred across all 1350 candidate evaluations in Stage 6
safe_wording: The software implementation executed 1350 candidate evaluations across 6 CTC backbones with exactly zero fail-closed runtime exceptions or crashes.
